items.title: Show HN: Disposable – Share small AI-made tools so others can rebuild them
items.summary: I made a site for sharing small tools made with AI. With agents, it is now quick to build a tool that fits your own task. But those tools usually get thrown away after use, and the next person who may needs something similar start again from zero. So I thought maybe if result or process could shared by text or code and this can lead to kind of token sharing economy. Its name is Disposable and compared to "Open source", I named its philosophy to "Open Disposable". So the principle is "Like open source, without the upkeep. I open-sourced an AI loop for RISC-V CPU design months prior to OpenAI
items.summary: Back in April, I built auto-arch-tournament (https://github.com/FeSens/auto-arch-tournament) to explore a question I’m still curious about: how well can different AI models improve a RISC-V CPU? I’ve been tracking the results on HWEBench(https://hwebench.com/v2). It’s fun to see OpenAI exploring a similar question in today’s chip design post(https://openai.com/index/advancing-chip-design-with-our-models/). If you’d like to try an experiment yourself, you can run the research loop from the repo.
